# Claude Code 2.1.325 record boundaries

Captured from a throwaway home on the declared secondary Claude subscription, using a private tmux server and the installed native 2.1.325 executable. No personal or office conversation was opened. The crew's program was not updated.

The four cumulative turn fixtures were produced by these short prompts:

- `Reply OK.`
- `Run true with Bash, then reply OK.`
- `Try Bash false once, then stop.` with `Bash(false)` denied in the throwaway settings.
- `Run sleep 30.` followed by Escape after the tool call was recorded. The native tool had already returned an error before the interrupt marker; this fixture proves interruption of the turn, not cancellation of an executing shell command.

Only fields needed by the record reader remain. Dates and message/tool identities are synthetic. Assistant prose, tool arguments/results, account identities, native paths, usage counters and API request bodies were removed. The native `[Request interrupted by user]` marker remains because it is the terminal evidence being tested. These fixtures do not preserve parent-history topology for compaction accounting.

`activity-metadata.jsonl` keeps one type tag for each non-input metadata kind observed. The expanded capture exercised Remote Control, compaction and resume, a local slash skill, queued input, a harmless local MCP ping tool, a hook that wrote its own marker, and an Opus 5.5/max turn with extended thinking. `bridge-session` and `cost-state` appeared in that expanded capture and are already recognized by the reader. All captured root kinds were already recognized at the base of this change; this is not evidence that an unidentified row kind from another conversation has been fixed.

`queued-prompt.jsonl` preserves the observed `queue-operation` enqueue of `Reply QUEUED.`, its dequeue without a content field, and the later native user echo and completed turn. An identity-free dequeue alone does not prove acceptance of any particular text.

A separate throwaway framework seat on the same pinned executable completed a short order, proved known idle through the ordinary idle reader, and accepted a fresh start. The live capture and its private evidence stay outside the repository.

`artifact-bookkeeping.jsonl` is entirely synthetic, built from the permitted key shapes of `frame-link` (both the saved artifact count and publication-link form), `artifact-comment-monitor`, and `artifact-autoreact-ledger`. The explicit classification is turn-neutral bookkeeping: none of these rows carries an input, a call, or a result. All identifiers, URLs, paths, titles and account values in that fixture are made up. The reader recognizes exactly these additional kind names; every other unmeasured kind remains unknown. Tests interleave the count between `atis-latch` and `bridge-session`, and the publication rows between an assistant/API row and the subsequent result, then after the completed turn.

`test_claude_2325_parallel.py` builds synthetic fixtures for a later isolated capture on the same executable and subscription. One API message made three independent Bash calls, emitted as separate native assistant rows: two foreground commands and one explicit background command. Its result returned `backgroundTaskId`; a notification enqueue, identity-free dequeue and user task notification started the following turn. The user origin had exactly `kind=task-notification`, `producer=session-task` and a nonempty `runId`. Two `ai-title` rows had exactly the keys `type`, `aiTitle` and `sessionId`. Six API request blob rows contained wire copies. The synthetic cases also combine the parallel calls into one assistant row, reverse the foreground result order and place copied results before native calls. No native ids, prompt/reply text, command arguments, results, titles or account data are retained in these fixtures. Only the measured call/result and enqueue/user carriers were added for this version; TaskStop, task-status attachments, remove and queued-command attachment carriers were not measured by this capture.

`test_claude_2325_background_lifetime.py` recreates a subsequent private capture: two explicit background Bash calls completed while a third foreground call kept the turn open. Each terminal notification first appeared on an enqueue, then on a `remove` with `reason=absorbed_mid_turn`, and on an attachment with `type=queued_command`, `commandMode=task-notification`, `origin={kind:task-notification, producer:session-task}` and a separate `runId`. The attachment retained its original enqueue timestamp, preceding the remove timestamp. Both remove and queued-command attachment are now measured at 2.1.325 as well as 2.1.317; 2.1.322 remains unmeasured for those forms. The earlier user-string notification capture remains the basis for that carrier. Synthetic watch cases use the exact absolute command extracted from the generated seat brief and a live registration bound to the synthetic launch; only that one watch is set aside by the existing idle view. The framework also gives the bare command in its waking line and check brief, so that candidate remains supported; the existing registration, generation, proof and live launch-descendant process decide the resting-watch exception. The bare-command attribution reader and check prompt are unchanged.

The fourth carrier was described by a structural diagnostic run by the owner of a private record, with names/types/booleans/counts only returned through the captain. Twenty 2.1.325 user tool results had exactly `content`, `is_error`, `tool_use_id`, `type`; each named a known foreground call, had a plain string with mixed output/notice text, and a row-level `toolUseResult`. Some were appended notices, others ordinary output quoting notice opening words. The synthetic regression therefore treats those strings solely as foreground results: a tag in tool output neither ends a background task nor invalidates one already ended on enqueue. No tool-result notice carrier or version set was added, and no private record was opened by the builder.

`background-running.json` is a synthetic copy of the `task_status` restoration attachment measured in a subsequent isolated native 2.1.325 capture. A 360-second explicit background Bash command remained running while `/compact` restored the conversation's context. The attachment had `type=task_status`, `taskType=local_bash`, `status=running`, string `taskId`, `description`, `outputFilePath`, null `deltaSummary`, and `shell` with string `command`, `kind`, `toolUseId`. The fixture replaces the timestamp, identities, command, description and path. This measures only the running-status version, not additional stop/resume forms. Timing contracts also recreate the owner-reported carrier order with synthetic values: call, result, terminal enqueue, remove and a matching attachment stamped before the enqueue but not before the task start. Such a measured copy leaves the ended task unchanged; a different status, wrong task, pre-start timestamp or unmeasured carrier remains invalid. The early-enqueue timestamp exception is deliberately absent.

`rest-*.txt` and `working-*.txt`, here and in `../2.1.317/`, are synthetic screens in the shapes measured on the ship's own seats on 15 November 2026 through `qd --json watch`: the composer's rules and box, a status row and the bottom line, with a working sign above the composer in the working ones. 2.1.317 was read on the crew's and the office's seats: nothing in the background, one shell, two shells, and one shell beside one monitor; a working sign under a minute with the glyph `✽`, and one past the first minute. 2.1.325 was read on the desk's seat, the only one on that version: the same bodies followed by the name of the session's published page, and, with a helper agent started in the background for the capture, the agents' panel below the line. Every reply, name, verb and token count in them is synthetic; only the program's own fixed words and marks are kept.
